data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Aruja is the wife of Indra, the god of rain. She is also known as Indrani and is the goddess of love, fertility, and nourishment. Aruja is believed to bestow blessings of prosperity, happiness, and longevity. The name Aruja carries the meaning “She who nourishes” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Aruja usually hope their child will grow to embody she who nourishes and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aruja total 6, giving a life-path number of 6. Number 6 is linked with Venus and with the qualities of responsibility, care and community.

Hindu festivals like Teej and Raksha Bandhan are dedicated to Aruja, signifying the importance of marital love and the harmony between brothers and sisters. The name Aruja is believed to bring blessings of good fortune, prosperity, and happiness to the bearer and those around them.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, Aruja is believed to be a symbol of the divine feminine and the power of love and nourishment. She represents the divine consort of Indra and embodies the grace, beauty, and compassion of a intercessor deity. Aruja's devotees seek her blessings for love, fertility, and prosperity in their lives. Her spiritual significance transcends the material world and connects individuals with the deeper realms of love, compassion, and the divine expression of the universe.
